subject: SIZE FIRST (USER s376): can PCL name a compiled CL closure? — the `subname` family, 1575 board rows behind it
description:
USER-approved s376: MEASURE before implementing.  Do NOT start the registry
until this sizing lands.

THE PRIZE: Scalar-List-Utils exotic_names.t is 1554 rows and subname.t is 21,
both FAIL at 0 ok today.  Both are blocked on the same thing —
lib/Sub/Util.pm's `subname` returns the literal '__ANON__' and `set_subname`
returns the code ref unchanged, because PCL cannot rename a compiled CL
closure.  (That stub is load-bearing for a SECOND reason, documented in the
file: merely DEFINING set_subname flips Sub::Defer's _CAN_SUBNAME to true,
which is what makes Moo's lazy/subclassed constructor bootstrap work.  Any
change here must keep that.)

THE MEASUREMENT (this task's whole deliverable):
 1. Can a function-object -> Perl-name registry answer subname()?  PCL
    already keeps %pcl-cl-sub-name in the other direction (see
    project_method_dispatch_subname_hoist).  Check whether an EQ hash keyed
    on the CL function object, populated at pl-sub definition time and at
    set_subname, is enough — and what it costs on the hot path (nothing, if
    writes are the only touch).
 2. Of exotic_names.t's 1554 rows, how many need only a NAME, and how many
    need the exotic part — stash names containing NUL, newline, latin-1,
    utf8?  Run the file under perl and bucket its descriptions.  If the
    exotic half dominates, the honest answer may be "21 rows + whatever
    subname.t's siblings buy", not 1575.
 3. What else pays: caller() reports the sub name (#233 wants 4 elements and
    real names), %DB::sub, and Sub::Util's own contract.

Write the answer beside the task and bring it back before writing code.
